job.title: National Corporate Account Manager | Workspaces
job.description:
Strategic National Accounts | Property & Workplace Solutions | Senior Client Relationships

The Company
Our client is a well-established Australian organisation operating across the commercial property, workplace and construction sectors. With a strong national presence and broad suite of solutions, they partner with some of Australia’s largest corporate organisations to deliver innovative workplace outcomes.

An opportunity now exists for an experienced National Corporate Account Manager to join their established national team and take ownership of strategic relationships with major enterprise clients.

The Opportunity
This is not a traditional project-based sales role. You’ll focus on building long-term, national relationships with major corporate end users, working with senior decision-makers across Property, Workplace, Facilities, Procurement, Design and Executive teams.

You will manage and grow existing strategic accounts while also identifying and securing new national clients, particularly large organisations operating across multiple states and locations. The focus is on getting ahead of upcoming projects, understanding clients’ longer-term workplace strategies and positioning solutions before opportunities formally come to market.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Develop and execute strategic growth plans across major national accounts
  • Build relationships with senior and C-Suite stakeholders across large corporate organisations
  • Grow existing accounts while proactively targeting new national clients
  • Identify future opportunities, workplace initiatives and client needs before projects hit the market
  • Negotiate national agreements, preferred supplier arrangements and commercial frameworks
  • Work closely with state-based sales teams to deliver a consistent national approach
  • Identify opportunities to cross-sell a broader range of workplace products and solutions
  • Maintain a strong pipeline and drive sustainable, long-term revenue growth
About You
We’re looking for a commercially minded relationship builder who understands how to navigate large, complex corporate accounts at a national level.
You will ideally bring:
  • 5+ years’ experience in national account management, business development or strategic sales
  • A strong existing network of national corporate relationships and decision-makers is key
  • Experience across workplace, commercial furniture, property, construction, property services or a related B2B environment
  • Demonstrated experience developing and growing major enterprise accounts
  • Confidence engaging with senior executives and C-Suite stakeholders
  • A strategic approach to sales – someone who can look beyond the immediate project and identify longer-term opportunities
  • Strong commercial, communication and stakeholder management skills.
This is an excellent opportunity for an established national sales professional looking to take ownership of significant corporate relationships and play a key role in the continued growth of a leading Australian business.

For any questions relating to this role or other opportunities with D&B and our clients please contact Renee Hamilton at rhamilton@designandbuild.com.au or click apply. Your application will be treated as strictly confidential.

job.title: Receptionist/Admin Assistant
job.description:
Join a well-established residential builder known for quality homes, exceptional service and a strong team culture. Based in a modern office, this is a great opportunity for someone looking to build their career in administration and residential construction.

Key Responsibilities
  • Create a warm and professional first impression for clients and visitors
  • Support the wider team with day-to-day administration
  • Answer and direct incoming calls and enquiries
  • Assist with CRM updates, new deals and reporting
  • Coordinate meeting rooms, refreshments and office requirements
  • Assist with building permits and general documentation

job.title: Coordinator Fleet and Urban Maintenance
job.description:
About Baw Baw Shire Council

Baw Baw Shire Council is a growing municipality located on the doorstep of metropolitan Melbourne, encompassing thriving townships, rural communities and some of Gippsland’s most attractive natural landscapes.
  
With continued growth placing increasing demand on Council services and infrastructure, Baw Baw is focused on building the capability, systems and services required to support its communities into the future.
  
This creates an exciting opportunity for an experienced operational leader to join the Open Space & Maintenance team and play an important role in how Council’s fleet and urban maintenance services continue to evolve.
  
About the Role

Reporting to the Manager Open Space & Maintenance, you will provide leadership across Council’s Fleet, Workshop and Urban Maintenance functions, with responsibility for a diverse in-house workforce of approximately 20 employees.
  
You will oversee services spanning Council’s fleet and plant, workshop operations, drainage and footpath maintenance, signage, street sweeping and public amenity cleansing.
  
A key focus of the role will be people leadership. You will support and develop your supervisors, create clarity around expectations and priorities, and continue building a collaborative and accountable culture across the depot.
  
Alongside the operational leadership, you will bring a strategic lense to how these services are planned and managed. This includes strengthening governance, systems and performance reporting, managing risk and compliance, and identifying opportunities to improve service delivery as the municipality continues to grow.
  
Fleet will form an important part of the portfolio, with Council managing approximately 450 vehicles and plant across operational, pool, commuter and private-use arrangements. You will oversee long-term fleet and replacement planning, workshop capability, lifecycle management and investment decisions to ensure Council’s fleet remains safe, compliant and financially sustainable.
  
The role will also provide strategic oversight across urban maintenance, ensuring appropriate service standards, maintenance programs and systems are in place across drainage, footpaths, signage, street sweeping and cleansing.
  
About You

We are looking for an experienced operational leader who combines strong people leadership with the ability to take a broader view of service delivery, risk and continuous improvement.
  
Experience leading operational services within a complex environment will be important, with exposure to fleet, asset management or municipal maintenance highly regarded. This is less about being a technical specialist across every area and more about bringing strong leadership and a broader strategic perspective.
  
Strong people leadership will be central to success. An approachable, practical and collaborative style, combined with experience developing supervisors and operational teams, managing performance and creating clear accountability, will be highly valued.
  
A sound understanding of fleet or asset lifecycle management, operational governance, safety and risk will be important, along with the commercial awareness to manage budgets, procurement and external service providers. Experience with heavy vehicle or Chain of Responsibility requirements will be advantageous, or alternatively the ability to quickly develop this knowledge.
  
Strong communication and stakeholder skills will complement the ability to balance day-to-day operational priorities with longer-term planning and continuous improvement.
  
Relevant tertiary qualifications in asset management, business, engineering, leadership, governance, project management or a related discipline, combined with substantial relevant experience, will be required.
  
Application Process

Public Sector People is partnering with Baw Baw Shire Council to recruit this opportunity on behalf of the Open Space & Maintenance team.
  
For a confidential discussion or to request a copy of the position description, please contact Blanche Grimaux at Public Sector People.
  
To apply, please submit your CV and a brief cover letter via the link.
  
Applications close Tuesday 6th October at 5pm.

Rather than transactional or project-by-project sales, you’ll take a longer-term approach – understanding clients' national property and workplace portfolios, developing multi-year account strategies and identifying opportunities well before they formally come to market.

You’ll work with senior stakeholders across Property, Workplace, Facilities, Procurement, Design, People & Culture and Executive teams, while partnering with internal state-based teams to deliver a coordinated national approach.

job.title: A06 WHS Assurance / Wellbeing / Compliance
job.description:
Public Sector People are working with the QLD State Government Department, who are seeking multiple experienced A06 WHS Project Officer officers on a temporary 6-month contract with opportunity to extend.

Overview:
  • ASAP START
  • Initial 6-month contract (+extension)
  • A06 WHS Project Officer (positions listed below)
  • Attractive pay rates from $78 p/h + 12% Super (PAYG)
  • QLD State Government
  • Brisbane Northern Suburbs
  • On site parking | WFH up to two days per week
  
Positions on offer:
  • Senior Project Officer - WHS Governance & Compliance
  • Senior Project Officer - Health & Wellbeing
  • Senior Project Officer - WHS Systems & Assurance

Through undertaking a significant period of transformation, with major investments being made in governance, health and wellbeing, risk management and safety systems across the organisation.
  
This organisation is focused on building contemporary frameworks, strengthening compliance obligations and creating a proactive safety culture that supports both paid personnel and volunteers.
  
Workplace Health and Safety sits at the centre of this transformation, with these roles playing a critical part in shaping the systems, programs and governance structures that will protect the workforce and drive organisational performance well into the future.
  
Senior Project Officer - WHS Governance & Compliance:

This role is focused on strengthening WHS governance, compliance frameworks and risk management practices . The position is responsible for driving improvements to the organisation's WHS Management System and ensuring consistent governance processes are implemented statewide.
  • Coordinate and support Tier 1 and Tier 2 WHS Governance Committees.
  • Lead implementation of ISO 45001 and ISO 45003 audit recommendations.
  • Drive improvements to the WHS Management System (WHSMS).
  
Senior Project Officer - Health & Wellbeing:

This role is centred on worker health, medical standards and wellbeing initiatives, with a significant focus on implementing new medical standards across Rural Services  and delivering key health monitoring programs.
  • Support implementation of revised medical standards frameworks.
  • Support fatigue management, heat stress and manual handling projects.
  • Provide health and wellbeing project support across operational workforces.
  
Senior Project Officer - WHS Systems & Assurance:

This role focuses on WHS assurance, reporting, systems improvement, compliance monitoring and organisational data management. It is aimed at creating the frameworks and systems required to measure WHS performance and drive continuous improvement.
  • Develop and implement the WHS Assurance Framework.
  • Establish assurance and review mechanisms for WHS compliance.
  • Support ongoing implementation and optimisation of the Integrum WHS system.
  
What we are looking for:
  • Certificate IV or higher in Workplace Health and Safety.
  • Experience delivering complex projects within government, emergency services, health or regulated environments.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
  • Experience developing policies, frameworks or programs.
  • Understanding of WHS legislation and contemporary safety practices.
  • Strong governance, reporting and problem-solving capabilities.
  • Experience balancing multiple priorities while achieving project outcomes
  
*** This is a competitive role and the client is looking to move quick***
  
As an approved Government recruitment partner Public Sector People are ideally placed to assist you in your search for your next temporary or permanent opportunity.
  
Best of luck!

job.title: Senior Power Systems Engineer
job.description:
Position: Senior Power Systems Engineer
Location: Sydney
Salary: $160k-$190k base

Join a leading Australian EPC contractor with a strong in-house engineering team delivering major HV substation, transmission and renewable energy projects.

This is a specialist Power Systems role focused on the core studies and reports that underpin the detailed design of HV substations.

Rather than studying how different scenarios impact the wider network, you’ll be working directly alongside Primary, Secondary & Protection and LV Engineering teams, with your studies feeding into the design, equipment selection and delivery of their projects.

Why this role?
  • National offices in Sydney, Melbourne & Adelaide 
  • Genuine specialist in-house EPC engineering team
  • Major pipeline across substations, transmission, BESS and renewable energy nationally 
  • Work across the full project lifecycle from detailed design through to construction and commissioning
  • Opportunity to help grow inhouse Power Systems capability
What you’ll be doing
  • Deliver the core power systems studies that underpin HV substation design
  • Perform load flow and short circuit studies
  • Complete insulation coordination and TRV studies
  • Perform arc flash, harmonic and power quality assessments
  • Assess transformer loading and system balancing
  • Develop detailed power system models using DIgSILENT PowerFactory
  • Interpret study results and provide recommendations that directly inform substation design and equipment selection
  • Prepare technical reports, calculations and study findings
  • Provide engineering support through design, construction and commissioning
What we’re looking for
  • 5+ years’ electrical engineering experience
  • Strong Power Systems studies experience supporting detailed HV substation design
  • Hands-on DIgSILENT PowerFactory experience
  • Strong understanding of how power system studies influence substation design and equipment selection
  • Degree qualified in Electrical Engineering
  • Engineers Australia membership or eligibility
  • CPEng or working towards is highly regarded
  • Strong understanding of Australian power utility standards and requirements
Apply now or contact Jasmine on 0405 437 667 for a confidential discussion.

Work a 35-hour week with flexible start and finish times around our core hours of 9am–12pm and 2pm–4pm.

Years of Service Leave
Receive an additional day of leave for every year worked, capped at 5 additional days per year.

Additional support on top of the Australian Government Paid Parental Leave Scheme, including salary top-ups for eligible primary carers, plus additional paid leave for both primary and secondary carers.

High Achiever Rewards

Compassionate Leave

Christmas Closure
We close our offices over the Christmas period — in addition to your accrued annual leave entitlements.

Flexible Annual Leave
Need a holiday before you've accrued enough leave? We allow employees to go into a reasonable negative leave balance.

Flexible Work Attire
Forget the suit and tie. Dress professionally and appropriately for your day — while being ready for any last-minute client or candidate meeting.

Build Your Career With Us This is more than an entry-level job.
We’ll give you the training, tools and support to build a genuine career in recruitment, with a clear pathway to becoming a successful 360 Consultant, Senior Consultant and beyond.

You’ll have the opportunity to build your own market, develop long-term relationships, grow your network and directly influence your earning potential and career progression.

job.title: Director Infrastructure Services
job.description:
Director - Infrastructure Services
Build trust. Grow people. Deliver infrastructure that lasts.
The Hawkesbury is unlike anywhere else in metropolitan Sydney - and this is an opportunity to lead work that residents can see, use and value for generations.

Across approximately 2,776 square kilometres, Hawkesbury City Council is the custodian of an infrastructure asset portfolio valued at approximately $1.69 billion. Its road network includes 799 kilometres of sealed roads and 278 kilometres of unsealed roads across townships and rural villages.

We are looking for a Director who understands that infrastructure leadership is about more than delivering projects. It is about earning trust, developing people, making good decisions and creating lasting community value.

The opportunity
Reporting to the General Manager, you will join Council's Senior Executive Team and lead approximately 170 employees across asset management, capital delivery, infrastructure operations, waste and resource recovery, plant and fleet, and emergency management.

You will oversee a capital works program of approximately $120 million, including major road, building and community infrastructure projects.

The challenge is significant: strengthen asset management maturity, deliver an ambitious program, improve infrastructure resilience and transition from considerable grant-funded investment to a sustainable long-term program.

This is not a role for someone arriving with a fixed 'been there, done that' mindset. We want a leader who remains curious, develops themselves and others, challenges established thinking constructively and relentlessly pursues better community value.

What you will lead
  • Deliver major projects while strengthening cost, contract and program discipline.
  • Improve asset planning, data, prioritisation and lifecycle management.
  • Build resilient and sustainable infrastructure.
  • Develop managers, grow internal capability and create long-term succession.
  • Lead professional, operational and field-based teams with clarity and respect.
  • Build credibility with Councillors, employees, government partners and a highly engaged community.
  • Turn Council's values - Healthy, Efficient, Accountable, Respectful and Team Focused - into visible leadership behaviours.
What you will bring You may already be an experienced Director, or you may be an exceptional senior Manager or Executive Manager ready to step up. Your background could be in local or state government, an infrastructure owner, utility, consultancy or another complex asset-intensive organisation.

Essentially, you will bring:
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in engineering, construction, project management or a related discipline.
  • Extensive senior leadership experience in a complex statutory or regulated environment.
  • Strategic judgement and the confidence to operate in a political and community-facing setting.
  • Strong budgeting, cost-control, performance, project and contract-management capability.
  • Experience leading change, continuous improvement and a large multidisciplinary workforce.
  • Strong governance, probity, communication and stakeholder-management skills.
  • A genuine commitment to safety, wellbeing, inclusion and respectful leadership.
  • The resilience and adaptability to lead through competing priorities and changing circumstances.
  • Local government executive and emergency-management experience would be advantageous but is not essential.
The offer
The total remuneration package is $305,000-$315,000. The position is based at Council Chambers Administration Building in Windsor. Following the six-month probation period, Council's hybrid arrangement requires three days in the office and allows up to two days working from home.

Council is an equal opportunity employer. Hawkesbury City Council values a diverse and inclusive workplace representing the community we serve.
Public Sector People is committed to an accessible recruitment process. If you require support to participate in the process, please contact Alex Scott.

Start a confidential conversation If you want to lead visible, meaningful work and leave the Hawkesbury stronger for the future, we would welcome a conversation. To apply, submit your resume and a concise cover letter outlining your motivation and relevant experience.
